articles.title: Bill Gates' $3.9 million-a-week superyacht has one rule that forces guests off for six hours
articles.standfirst: A dream superyacht, amenities beyond imagination and one unusual feature few would expect to find on a vessel of this caliber.
articles.summary: A dream superyacht, amenities beyond imagination and one unusual feature few would expect to find on a vessel of this caliber.
articles.body:
Imagining a vacation aboard Breakthrough means picturing an experience where seemingly nothing is missing. The 118.8-meter superyacht features ocean-view suites, balconies that extend over the water, a gym, sauna, private cinema and even an underwater lounge with windows offering views of marine life. Everything is designed for an extraordinary luxury getaway, with charter rates reaching $3.9 million per week .

But Breakthrough also has a rather unusual backstory. Its construction was originally commissioned by Bill Gates, Microsoft's co-founder, although he never actually stepped aboard once the superyacht was completed . Some time later, the vessel was acquired by Canadian billionaire Patrick Dovigi, an environmental services entrepreneur and former professional hockey goaltender.

However, beyond the man who commissioned its construction and the impressive amenities it offers, Breakthrough has one particular feature its guests need to keep in mind: whenever it's time to replenish the liquid hydrogen used by one of its power systems, everyone must leave the yacht for approximately six hours. It's a mandatory break that means leaving behind the suites, terraces and all those luxuries to continue the vacation on land.

Why can't anyone stay aboard during refueling?

It all comes down to the fuel used by one of the yacht's power systems. Breakthrough stores approximately four metric tons of liquid hydrogen in a cryogenic tank, which keeps it at a temperature close to -423 degrees Fahrenheit . This fuel requires very specific handling conditions because it can be highly flammable when it comes into contact with oxygen.

That's why refueling isn't an operation that can take place while guests continue enjoying the yacht's facilities. Before the process begins, a safety perimeter is established around the superyacht, and everyone must disembark. From that point on, the operation is handled by specialized personnel.

The process starts with purging the pipes with nitrogen and gradually cooling down the system. Only then does the fuel transfer begin. During this operation, excess gaseous hydrogen is released through a venting structure located on the mast, known as the needle.

So, no matter how much Breakthrough has to offer for an extraordinary vacation, there's one thing even its millions of dollars can't change: when it's time to refuel with hydrogen, everyone has to get off the yacht.

articles.title: Tiffani Thiessen, star of ‘Saved by the Bell,’ will undergo surgery for a hip replacement: “I’m like a German shepherd”
articles.standfirst: The actress shared it on her podcast ‘Breaking Bread with Tom Papa’
articles.summary: The actress shared it on her podcast ‘Breaking Bread with Tom Papa’
articles.body:
Actress Tiffani Thiessen , remembered for her role as Kelly Kapowski in ‘Saved by the Bell’ , revealed in November 2026 that she will have to undergo a hip replacement at age 52 after being diagnosed with hip dysplasia and a labral tear.

She herself revealed the news during her appearance on the podcast ‘Breaking Bread with Tom Papa’ . Initially, she learned that she had a labral tear (the ring of cartilage that surrounds the hip joint). However, after seeking a second medical opinion, she was also diagnosed with hip dysplasia , a condition in which the hip socket does not fully cover the ball-shaped upper part of the femur.

The intense pain has forced the actress to stop playing pickleball

Despite the painful diagnosis, the actress joked that, after learning she has dysplasia, she feels "basically like a German shepherd" , alluding to that dog breed’s well-known predisposition to suffering from this joint problem. “I’ve heard hip replacements aren’t as bad as knee and shoulder replacements” , she said with humor.

Thiessen, who was a dancer in her youth and maintains a very active lifestyle, explained that the intense pain has forced her to stop playing pickleball in recent weeks, a sport she usually plays with her 11-year-old son, Holt. “My doctor didn’t say it was pickleball, but it probably didn’t help. I haven’t been able to play in the last two weeks because my hip was really bad,” she said.

According to outlets such as Fox News and USA Today, the actress commented optimistically that she has heard that recovery from a hip replacement is usually easier than recovery from knee or shoulder surgery.

articles.title: Hoobastank turns FAA ground stop into an impromptu “The Reason” singalong
articles.summary: Hoobastank gave fellow passengers an unexpected live performance during Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop. The band played “The Reason” aboard a Southwest flight as travelers waited during the disruption.
articles.body:
Hoobastank gave fellow passengers an unexpected live performance during Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop. The band played “The Reason” aboard a Southwest flight as travelers waited during the disruption.

Frontman Doug Robb and a guitarist performed an acoustic version of the band’s 2004 hit. Passengers joined in, turning a frustrating travel delay into a plane-wide singalong.

The FAA ordered the ground stop on Nov. 13 after communication issues affected multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers. The agency later lifted the restriction, allowing departures to resume.

Videos of the performance spread on social media, giving travelers a memorable moment amid a day of flight disruptions across the United States.

articles.title: Bertrand Russell, philosopher: “Scientists make the impossible possible, politicians make the possible impossible”
articles.standfirst: A reflection by the British thinker on the differences between science and politics
articles.summary: A reflection by the British thinker on the differences between science and politics
articles.body:
Bertrand Russell was one of the most influential philosophers of the 20th century. A British mathematician, writer and thinker, he devoted much of his life to reflecting on society, knowledge, power and human behavior. His ideas, many of them centered on freedom of thought and critical thinking, continue to attract interest decades after his death.

Among his best-known reflections is a quote that directly contrasts the work of scientists with that of politicians: “Scientists strive to make the impossible possible. Politicians strive to make the possible impossible.” It is an irony-filled observation that highlights two very different ways of confronting challenges.

Science versus the limitations of politics, according to Bertrand Russell

The reflection draws a comparison between those who work to push the boundaries of knowledge and those responsible for managing public affairs. While scientists research, experiment and seek solutions to problems that once appeared to have no answer, politics is portrayed as a realm where obstacles can end up preventing things that should be possible from actually happening.

The quote also invites us to reflect on the expectations placed on public officials. Among politics’ main responsibilities are finding solutions, reaching agreements and enabling progress that benefits society. However, confrontation, competing interests and the difficulty of reaching consensus can become barriers to achieving those goals.

Russell, who died in 1970, championed the importance of reason, intellectual freedom and independent thought throughout his life. His philosophical legacy continues to influence debates on education, democracy and social organization. Through irony, this reflection encapsulates a criticism of the difficulties that can arise when those with the power to change things fail to turn possibilities into realities.

articles.title: Marlon Brando, Actor: "Trust your instincts over anyone else's advice"
articles.standfirst: Marlon Brando's rejection of the Oscar underscores the struggle of aligning personal beliefs with social justice, a challenge that resonates in today's celebrity activism landscape.
articles.summary: Marlon Brando's rejection of the Oscar underscores the struggle of aligning personal beliefs with social justice, a challenge that resonates in today's celebrity activism landscape.
articles.body:
Marlon Brando 's profound influence in cinema continues to resonate today, particularly as we navigate a world marked by hyperconnectivity and the pressures of societal expectations. His work, especially in pieces like Interview, illuminates the struggle of self-discovery, capturing the feeling of being lost amidst overwhelming stimuli and the incessant comparison with others. Brando's insight, "Trust your instincts over anyone else's advice," highlights the importance of personal growth and self-acceptance in an era where external validation often overshadow one’s own values and beliefs.

In contemporary society, the fear of making mistakes and the pressure to adhere to societal norms exacerbate feelings of inadequacy and isolation. Brando's life mirrors these challenges, emphasizing the need for resilience and the value of embracing one's journey, even amidst uncertainty and rapid change. His legacy reminds us that true fulfillment arises not from conformity but from understanding and accepting who we are, a relevant lesson in an age where individuality is constantly challenged by societal benchmarks.

Trust your instincts over anyone else's advice.

To understand the feeling of being lost in life, Marlon Brando's perspective offers an especially intriguing lens. His emphasis on the importance of self-discovery and personal growth aligns with the struggles many face today in pursuing authenticity and direction. Brando’s method acting approach not only revolutionized the film industry but also serves as a poignant reminder of the journey towards understanding one’s true self. By immersing himself deeply in his roles, he highlighted the significance of personal reflection, urging others to embrace their paths of self-exploration and growth.

Marlon Brando: Trusting Instincts in Acting

Marlon Brando, a seminal figure in American cinema, transformed the landscape of acting with his innovative methods and powerful performances. Born on April 3, 1924, in Omaha, Nebraska, Brando rose to stardom in the 1950s through iconic roles in "A Streetcar Named Desire," "On the Waterfront," and "The Godfather." Renowned for his extraordinary talent, he earned multiple awards, including two Academy Awards for Best Actor. Brando's legacy is not only marked by his cinematic achievements but also by his rejection of traditional film norms and advocacy for social justice, particularly noted in his refusal to accept the Oscar for "The Godfather."

Brando's approach to acting, heavily influenced by Stella Adler and the Stanislavski system, emphasized emotional authenticity and immersive character work. His method acting techniques have had a profound impact on generations of actors, shaping the craft as it is understood today. Collaborations with luminaries like Elia Kazan and Tennessee Williams further anchored his significance in the artistic community. The evolution of his career, alongside the works of contemporaries and predecessors, highlights a broader conversation about authenticity in performance—a theme explored by other greats such as Al Pacino and Jack Nicholson, who credit Brando's influence in their own style and approach.

One of Brando’s notable quotes, “Trust your instincts over anyone else's advice,” encapsulates his philosophy of self-trust and authenticity in both acting and personal life. This assertion serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of self-guidance and intuition, particularly in an industry where external opinions are abundant. Brando's own journey, filled with personal struggles and triumphs, reflects the challenges many face when navigating the expectations of society versus the call of one's true self. In essence, his words encourage individuals to find confidence within, drawing a vital connection between self-acceptance and success.

In the 21st century, the relevance of Brando's advice is palpable across various aspects of life. For individuals grappling with career decisions in a fast-paced world, the fear of conforming to others’ expectations can be paralyzing. Embracing Brando’s perspective invites a more introspective approach, urging people to reflect on their instincts instead of yielding to external pressures. This shift not only applies to actors facing the challenges of authenticity but resonates universally, encouraging everyone—from students to professionals— to trust their inner voice in pursuit of their aspirations amidst societal noise.

articles.title: Michael J. Fox and 35 Years of Battling Parkinson's: Here's How He Spent the Evening with His Family at the Gala
articles.standfirst: The actor hosted the 26th edition of his foundation's charity event in New York, accompanied by his wife, Tracy Pollan, and three of his four children.
articles.summary: The actor hosted the 26th edition of his foundation's charity event in New York, accompanied by his wife, Tracy Pollan, and three of his four children.
articles.body:
Michael J. Fox attended the annual gala for his foundation, “A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Cure Parkinson’s,” held at the Waldorf Astoria in New York on Saturday, November 14. The actor, who was diagnosed with Parkinson’s in 1991, was accompanied by his wife, Tracy Pollan, and their daughters Esmé, Aquinnah, and Schuyler.

The family posed together on the red carpet during the 26th edition of the event, organized to raise funds for research into the disease. Fox, 65, and Pollan, whom he has been married to since 1988, spent the evening with guests from the entertainment industry and supporters of the foundation.

Tracy Pollan spoke about life with the actor and his battle with Parkinson’s

During an interview with PEOPLE, Pollan explained how the family copes with the challenges of living with the disease. “I think you just have to take it one day at a time. You have to look at what’s in front of you and stay in the moment. If that moment is okay, that’s where you are,” she said.

The actress also highlighted the work the foundation has done for more than two decades and the importance of the resources allocated to scientists. “We’re really seeing a lot of progress,” she noted, referring to research aimed at improving treatments and finding a cure.

The Michael J. Fox Foundation has already allocated more than $3 billion to research

Fox was diagnosed in 1991, when he was 29, but did not go public with his illness until 1998. In 2000, he founded The Michael J. Fox Foundation , an organization that has since allocated more than $3 billion to fund Parkinson’s research.

This year’s gala featured Denis Leary as host, musical performances by John Mayer and Brad Paisley, and comedy acts by Josh Johnson and Tom Papa. The event marked its 26th edition and brought together people connected to the foundation and scientific research.

In September, Fox had spoken with PEOPLE about the progress he sees in the search for a cure. “We don’t know exactly when it will happen, but it will happen,” he said at the time, with complete conviction. He also mentioned new medications, scientific advances, and tools that help accelerate researchers’ work.

Science is difficult. It’s astronomically expensive. It requires time and collaboration. But as long as we stay focused and hopeful, we’ll get there. And science shows that we’re close. Every year we see more progress in research, new drugs to improve patients’ quality of life, and better tools for scientists to move forward more quickly.

The actor remains committed to leading the organization that bears his name, while continuing to support research into a disease he has been living with for 35 years. The gala on November 14 once again brought together his family and the foundation’s collaborators around that goal.

articles.title: Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber put up for sale the house of their son Presley, who died two months ago, for $3.6 million
articles.standfirst: The couple has made this decision with great pain
articles.summary: The couple has made this decision with great pain
articles.body:
Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber have decided to put up for sale the house that their late son Presley owned in the Hollywood Hills for $3.595 million (around €3.26 million) , almost two months after his death. Property records published by TMZ specify the details of the transaction.

The property went on the market on Friday, November 13. It is a mid-century home built in 1955, measuring around 280 square meters , located on a private lot of more than 2,000 square meters. It has four bedrooms, three bathrooms, a heated pool, jacuzzi, sauna, cold plunge area, and a separate guest house. Presley had purchased it in March 2023 for $3.4 million .

Cindy Crawford defines her son: “A sweet and beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever”

Presley Gerber died at the age of 27 last September 20 at the Resolutions Living rehabilitation center (Santa Monica), just one day after being admitted. Police continue to investigate the case as a suspected overdose with no signs of third-party involvement, pending confirmation of the final autopsy results.

After weeks of absolute silence and being seen collecting belongings from that residence, Cindy Crawford and her daughter Kaia shared emotional farewell messages on social media in mid-October, in which the model and actress thanked people for their expressions of affection and remembered her son as “a sweet and beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever” .

For her part, Kaia dedicated this message to her older brother: “I’ve read all the books and I have no answers. My ability to express myself is not up to this , to the magnitude of losing you... I am, literally, on my knees, completely devastated.”
